arguments.text:
For n=24t+1,t>=1,x=6t+1,b=nx: greedy completion exists iff b has a prime factor q=2 mod3. Necessity: (3y-b)(3z-b)=b^2 has positive factors, the first 2 mod3; if all primes of b are 1 mod3 this is impossible. Sufficiency: y=b(q+1)/(3q),z=q*y are integral, positive, and x<y<z since n>=25 and odd b forces q>=5. The q=5 subfamily is n=120s+97, x=30s+25, y=2n(6s+5), z=10n(6s+5), s>=0. General reasoning is a written proof, not a formal certificate or human-reviewed result. Independent finite audit: 416 cases,275 greedy successes,141 obstructions,zero criterion mismatches. Unrestricted finite replay exactly matches the old artifact hash and gives 9998 witnesses. Original conjecture unresolved; novelty not audited.
